blocks.title: Cis-trans isomers
blocks.text: Cis-trans isomers are stereoisomers with different spatial arrangements of atoms because rotation about a double bond in an open-chain compound is restricted.

First consider butane. Rotation about the C2-C3 single bond turns one arrangement of the methyl groups into another. Such forms are conformational isomers: they interconvert freely by rotation about the C-C single bond and cannot be separated at room temperature.

In but-2-ene, CH3-CH=CH-CH3, carbons 2 and 3 are sp2 hybridised. The C=C double bond consists of a sigma bond, formed by end-on overlap of sp2 hybrid orbitals, and a pi bond, formed by sideways overlap of p orbitals. The pi bond locks the molecule: the two carbons of the double bond and the groups attached to them lie in one plane and are fixed in space. To rotate about the double bond the pi bond would have to break, which needs about 263 kJ/mol, not available at room temperature. This restricted rotation is the origin of cis-trans isomerism.

blocks.alt: Top left: two sp2 carbons with upright p orbitals overlapping above and below the C-C bond to form the pi bond, each carbon carrying H and CH3. Top right: after a quarter turn of one carbon its p orbital lies flat and no longer overlaps. Bottom: cis-but-2-ene with both CH3 groups on the same side of C=C, and trans-but-2-ene with them on opposite sides.
blocks.caption: Restricted rotation about C=C in but-2-ene (original diagram after Figure 19.6).
blocks.long_description: The pi bond exists only while the two p orbitals are parallel. Turning one end of the molecule would destroy this overlap, so the groups on each carbon stay where they are. As a result cis-but-2-ene and trans-but-2-ene are separate compounds that do not change into each other at room temperature.

items: Cis isomer: the two similar groups are on the same side of the double bond (cis-but-2-ene).
Trans isomer: the two similar groups are on opposite sides (trans-but-2-ene).
Cis-trans isomerism is not possible if either carbon of the double bond carries two identical groups, e.g. but-1-ene (CH2=CH-CH2CH3) and 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene ((CH3)2C=C(CH3)2).

blocks.title: Condition for cis-trans isomerism
blocks.text: An open-chain compound shows cis-trans isomerism if it has a double bond and each carbon of the double bond carries two different groups.

blocks.title: Keep in mind
blocks.text: Cis and trans isomers have different physical and chemical properties: different melting and boiling points, dipole moments, densities and heats of vaporisation. The trans isomer is usually more stable than the cis isomer, so their reactivity differs too.
